<a id="mission"></a>

## Mission

You build TWO small units of plan 005-convo-ingest behind one seat: the omp-native reader (session jsonl, xd:// tool remap, toolCall/toolResult pairing, compaction records) and the pij-ledger reader (events.ndjson, seq cursor, receipts). Both implement the frozen ConversationSource trait independently. The ledger is paired with omp because it is too small for its own dispatch — it is not an afterthought. You report to the PM, not to prime.

| u1 | MEASURED CORRECTION (b) — COMPACTION IS A FIRST-CLASS RECORD, NOT THE INJECTED USER TURN THE RECIPE'S GOTCHA 5 DESCRIBES. omp writes type=='compaction' carrying summary/shortSummary/tokensBefore/firstKeptEntryId, at line 184 of the fixture, with the injected continuation user turn at line 185 whose parentId equals the compaction record's id. It maps to a SYSTEM-SOURCE turn and is NEVER DROPPED — that is plan acceptance criterion ac-0005, and it is the single most likely thing to be silently lost, because the reference oracle drops it (read_omp handles only type=='message'). Its absence from the oracle subset is BY CONSTRUCTION; emitting it is required, not a divergence. |
| u2 | MEASURED CORRECTION (c) — AN OMP SESSION JSONL IS NOT PURELY APPEND-ONLY: line 0 is a fixed-width 256-byte title slot REWRITTEN IN PLACE. A byte-offset cursor survives this only because the slot's width never changes, and the rewrite is invisible to both the size check and the inode check. This is documented at the top of tail.rs; read it before you reason about the cursor. |
| u3 | MEASURED CORRECTION (d) — TOOL NAMING IS ASYMMETRIC: omp names a tool under `name` on the CALL and `toolName` only on the paired RESULT, and a tool_execution_start mirror precedes every call, so a naive tool count DOUBLES. The fixture has all 72 toolResult records carrying toolCallId + toolName, and all 72 match a toolCall block exactly once — zero orphans either way. Pair on toolCallId; prove the zero-orphan property in a test. |
| u4 | RECIPE GOTCHA 2 — xd:// REMAP: omp encodes in-process tools as virtual `write` toolCalls whose arguments.path starts with `xd://`. The fixture has them at lines 105 (two in one assistant record), 125 and 174, plus a `read` at 93. These are tool invocations, not file writes; a reader that reports them as writes will fill the index with fictional file edits. |
| u5 | THE PIJ LEDGER'S SUBSET EXPECTATION IS WEAK, AND IT IS LABELLED WEAK — do not read a passing subset check as proof. The oracle yields only 3 turns from 50 records (it emits solely receipt and message events, keeps only role user/assistant, and needs a text block; this harvested window is tool-heavy — 13 of its 14 text blocks sit on role 'toolResult' and every assistant record is thinking + toolCall with no prose). The STRUCTURAL claim is this store's real done-bar. The fixture was harvested to cover the seq cursor and the two receipt records (lines 5 and 10, seq 122 queued/non-delivered and seq 127 delivered) — cover those. |
| u6 | CURSORS DIFFER BETWEEN YOUR TWO READERS AND THAT IS THE POINT: omp resumes on SourceCursor::ByteOffset{device,inode,offset}, the ledger on SourceCursor::Seq{seq}. The contract suite's foreign-cursor case requires each reader to REFUSE the other's variant rather than silently read it as zero. |
| u7 | LINE FRAMING IS ALREADY BUILT AND TESTED — use crates/providers/src/conversation_sources/tail.rs (`read_lines`) for both readers; do not write two more tail buffers. Spend this unit on the two DIALECTS. If tail.rs is missing something, stop-and-ask the PM. |
